You are adversarially verifying an audit finding about the mootdx project at /workspace.

FINDING
  symbol: mootdx.utils.demjson._nonnumber_float_constants
  kind:   missing
  detail: Spec item 46-59 names `_nonnumber_float_constants` as required surface of mootdx.utils.demjson. The function IS defined at /workspace/mootdx/utils/demjson.py:261, but line 630 executes `del _nonnumber_float_constants` immediately after `nan, inf, neginf = _nonnumber_float_constants()` on line 629, so the name is not accessible as a module attribute. CAVEAT: this is byte-for-byte upstream demjson 2.2.4 behaviour — I diffed the whole file against the published mootdx 0.11.7 wheel and sdist and it is AST-identical modulo docstrings, so this is a spec-checklist vs upstream disagreement, not an injected defect. Fix would be deleting line 630 (harmless; nan/inf/neginf are already bound).
  repro:  cd /workspace && python -c "from mootdx.utils.demjson import _nonnumber_float_constants"  # -> ImportError: cannot import name '_nonnumber_float_constants' from 'mootdx.utils.demjson' (/workspace/mootdx/utils/demjson.py);  also: python -c "import mootdx.utils.demjson as d; print(hasattr(d,'_nonnumber_float_constants'))" -> False

The authoritative spec checklist is /tmp/spec_checklist.md.
Run the repro yourself. Try hard to REFUTE the finding: maybe the symbol exists under a different but
still-importable path, maybe the spec text is loose pseudo-code rather than a literal requirement, maybe
the behaviour already matches. Default to real=false when uncertain or when the "gap" only exists in
spec prose that no plausible test could assert (e.g. a private inner function's exact name).
Set real=true only if a straightforward test written from the spec would fail today.
If real=true, give the minimal concrete fix (which file, what to add).
